title: Phylogeographical analyses of the water shrew Chimarrogale platycephalus (Soricidae: Eulipotyphala) based on genetic analysis of its faeces
content:
Abstract
The evolutionary history of Chimarrogale platycephalus, an endangered water shrew endemic to Japan, was investigated. The method of genetic analysis based on faecal specimens established in our previous study was adopted. The present study promoted a deeper discussion of additional specific phylogenetic evolutionary scenarios, introduction of ecological niche modelling and divergence period estimation. Regarding the history of the phylogenetic evolution of the water shrew, the following scenarios were clarified. First, during the Pleistocene, an ancestral group of C. platycephalus migrated from the Asian Continent to Kyushu, and then to Honshu, expanding its distribution area in a southwest to northeast direction. During a period spanning the Calabrian to the Chibanian era, its distribution repeatedly contracted and expanded due to climate change. Its areas of distribution were reduced during glacial periods and expanded during interglacial periods. After differentiation into four genetic lineages from different refugia, two of these lineages are now in a state of secondary contact in Honshu. The distribution areas of these two lineages overlap over a wide area. This study investigated the genetic structures and evolutionary history of higher order predators in the ecosystems of Japanese streams and provides important results for conservation genetics.
